summary: This bill requires the Office of Management and Budget to update guidelines within one year so federal agencies must use the best reasonably available evidence when developing or explaining rules and guidance, disclose the critical factual material they rely on in public dockets or records, and handle public correction requests for that material.

scores.thoughts: The bill includes an explicit 'no additional funds' clause prohibiting new appropriations to implement its requirements. This prevents any expansion of spending while directing agencies to improve information quality processes using existing resources. The connection is tangential at best and does not restructure or cut any existing programs.
The bill contains no provisions related to tax rates, tax policy, revenue collection, or any tax-related matters.
The bill is a general procedural statute applying to all federal agencies and does not address healthcare delivery, insurance, public coverage, or market-based reforms.
No provisions in the bill address firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill does not mention immigration, border policy, visas, or related enforcement mechanisms.
No language in the bill pertains to reproductive health services, abortion access, or restrictions.
The bill makes no changes to defense authorizations, military budgets, or national security spending.
While the bill's evidence-quality rules would apply to environmental agencies, it does not create, expand, or limit any environmental regulations or protections.
The legislation does not alter eligibility, funding, or administration of welfare, nutrition assistance, or other safety-net programs.
No provisions address schools, federal education funding, school choice, or curriculum policy.
The bill contains nothing related to drug scheduling, enforcement, decriminalization, or treatment programs.
No references to sentencing, policing, incarceration, or criminal justice reform appear in the text.
The bill does not address tariffs, trade agreements, or import/export policy.
The 'no additional funds' clause has a minor, indirect effect of avoiding new deficit spending, but the bill does not prioritize debt reduction or authorize deficit-financed investments.
The legislation does not expand or restrict legal protections or rights for LGBTQ+ individuals.
No provisions concern foreign assistance, international aid programs, or related funding.
The bill does not address voting access, election administration, voter ID, or campaign finance.

The bill requires public disclosure of certain factual materials used in rulemaking while explicitly preserving existing privacy protections under 5 U.S.C. §§ 552 and 552a. This creates a minor procedural interaction with data transparency but does not regulate technology companies or establish new privacy rules.
No provisions affect collective bargaining, worker protections, or union rights.
The bill does not address religious exemptions, civil rights enforcement, or conflicts between religious liberty and anti-discrimination rules.
